clue.text: Deep green?

parts.note: the deep is the sea, and green suggests a lawn's growth, so this is a green plant living in the deep

explanation.surface: A question about a very dark shade of green.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that 'Deep green' is not a colour: read 'deep' as the ocean and 'green' as a grassy plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine flowering plant growing in shallow coastal waters, the green growth of the deep.

clue.text: Time, that takes of all the world, Must have a stop. (Henry IV, Part 1)

definitions.text: Time, that takes of all the world, Must have a stop. (Henry IV, Part 1)

parts.words: Time, that takes of all the world, Must have a stop. (Henry IV, Part 1)
parts.note: a quotation from Hotspur's dying words with one word left out, between 'takes' and 'of'; the missing word is the answer

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's history play about time's ending.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a fill-in-the-blank clue: Hotspur's line runs 'But thought's the slave of life, and life time's fool; And time, that takes ___ of all the world, Must have a stop.'
explanation.definitionFit: Time takes a survey, an overall view or inspection, of the whole world in the quoted line.

clue.text: An order given in Northern Ireland

parts.note: trim means order or good condition, as in 'in good trim'

explanation.surface: A command issued somewhere in Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTRIM is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, so it is a place 'in Northern Ireland'.
explanation.definitionFit: County Antrim is a county in the north-east of Ulster, part of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Turning over gold ring, the holy man will get a place to sleep

indicators.note: turning over says the word for gold is flipped round to run backwards

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a ring is round like the letter O
ST is short for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A priest flips a golden ring and finds somewhere to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch where birds settle for the night, a resting spot.

clue.text: Marked in dates for settlement

indicators.note: settlement suggests the letters of the following words settling into a new order

explanation.surface: Something noted in the calendar for a financial settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for settlement' reads like accounting, but 'settlement' signals rearranging IN DATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Stained means discoloured or blotted, having marks on it.

clue.text: Totters when receiving divine queen

indicators.note: receiving means the word for when takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a divine or clergyman
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone staggers about while welcoming a holy royal visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totters' looks like a verb for staggering; read it as people who tot up figures.
explanation.definitionFit: People who tot up sums are those who add numbers together, a punning definition.

clue.text: Colouring as a result of complaint

definitions.meaning: a kind of water-based paint used on walls
a viral disease of dogs and other animals

explanation.surface: A tint caused by an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a type of wall paint and an infectious canine illness.

clue.text: Favour demonstration

parts.note: a public show of preference, where people express which candidate they favour by voting

explanation.surface: A rally showing support for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a street protest in favour of a cause; it is the formal vote by which a population shows its preference.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote choosing representatives is a formal display of which candidates the people prefer.

clue.text: A taste is allowed and is really gratifying

indicators.note: allowed hints that the letters are let loose and permitted to rearrange

explanation.surface: Being permitted a sample of something is deeply pleasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allowed' is the signal to rearrange A TASTE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To satiate is to satisfy fully, to gratify a desire to the limit.

clue.text: A liar not perhaps capable of reasoning

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A fibber who may not be able to think straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational describes a mind able to think logically and sensibly.

clue.text: A bouquet for the climber

parts.note: a bouquet is the scent or aroma of a wine

explanation.surface: Flowers presented to a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' suggests flowers but means an aroma, as with wine; the definition is something for the climber, a rise to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb upward is what a mountaineer makes, the way up the slope.

clue.text: In the sales some prices are of course lower

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: During a sale prices naturally drop.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the sentence is surface padding which also sums up the meaning: in the sales prices are lower.
explanation.definitionFit: Less means smaller in amount, reduced, as prices are when cut.

clue.text: That's Life broadcast-exit scene-shifters!

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered about, so the following letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A TV show title and a nod to stagehands who move scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's Life' was a BBC consumer television programme; here it simply says the answer is life. 'scene-shifters' adds a theatrical surface flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alive is to have being, the state of living.

clue.text: Offering some pretext, radioed for more

indicators.note: Offering some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone sends an excuse over the radio asking for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added beyond the usual is an additional amount, something more.

clue.text: Second-hand, but found serviceable

explanation.surface: An old item that still turned out to be useful.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both previously owned goods and having been employed for a purpose.

clue.text: Long story told with many acknowledgments of indebtedness, which is wise

parts.note: a saga is a long story, originally Norse
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
IOUs are written notes acknowledging a debt, 'I owe you'

explanation.surface: A long tale full of thanks turns out to be shrewd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acknowledgments of indebtedness' sounds like expressions of gratitude, but means IOUs, signed promises to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacious describes someone shrewd, with keen judgement.

clue.text: Take a certain attitude to drink, as one might guess

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in sips
a pose is a certain stance or attitude of the body

explanation.surface: Someone adopts a stance towards drinking, as you might expect.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess is to suppose, to assume something without proof.

clue.text: Court official making a suggestion to office-workers

parts.note: a tip is a useful hint or suggestion
the staff are the people employed in an office

explanation.surface: A court employee offering advice to clerks.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipstaff is a sheriff's officer or court usher, named after the metal-tipped staff once carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a court officer or bailiff carrying a staff of office.

clue.text: A European isn't a one to change

indicators.note: to change says the following letters must alter their order

explanation.surface: A continental who refuses to adapt.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Estonia, a Baltic country in northern Europe.

clue.text: Visible apprehension

definitions.meaning: split as two words, '...' means able to be seen
understanding or perception, grasping an idea

explanation.surface: Fear that can be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehension' looks like fear but here means understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is being in view; the second is deep understanding.

clue.text: Carry a little child-there's point to that

parts.note: a tot is a small child
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Lifting a toddler, with a moral to the story.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry something, especially something heavy.

clue.text: Cheese obtained by a scoundrel with a note

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: A villain gets some cheese along with a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Curd is the soft solid from soured milk, a simple fresh cheese.

clue.text: Hold back and read article in a vessel

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or read attentively

indicators.note: in places the article inside the word for the vessel

parts.note: a tin is a metal container or vessel
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Restraining someone and reading a piece in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a tin, a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain feelings is to restrain them, keeping them in check.

clue.text: Guides drink up, imbibing a great deal

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the word for drink swallows the other letters
up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: to sip is to drink in small mouthfuls
a lot means a great deal

explanation.surface: Tour leaders down their drinks and take in plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots steer or navigate, as when guiding a ship into harbour.

clue.text: Saw the male sovereign into bed

indicators.note: into means these letters are placed within the word for bed

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a sovereign is a gold coin worth one pound, abbreviated L from libra

explanation.surface: Watching a king being put to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests a monarch, but it is the British gold pound coin, giving L.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheld is the past tense of behold, to have looked at or seen.

clue.text: A philosopher's religious writings turned in as written

indicators.note: in places the turned writings within the word meaning as written

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation exactly as written

indicators.note: turned means the short form for scripture is turned around

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a body of religious writings

explanation.surface: A thinker's scriptures handed in exactly as composed.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the ancient Greek school founded by Zeno, teaching endurance without complaint.

clue.text: May be tried and seen to soften

indicators.note: may be suggests these words could be something else once their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something might be tested and examined in order to make it softer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tenderise meat is to make it softer by beating or marinating.

clue.text: A character expected to invest

parts.note: EN is the spelt-out name of the letter N, a character
due means expected, as in 'the train is due'

explanation.surface: A figure who is anticipated to put money in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' suggests finance, but here means endow or clothe with a quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or furnish someone with a quality, an old sense of investing.

clue.text: Woman with a son about 51

indicators.note: about means the other words go around the number

parts.note: son is taken as written
LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A mother with a boy who is in his fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, an example of a female name.

clue.text: Liberal's part taken by the workman

indicators.note: taken by means the word for part is attached to the workman

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in a farmhand
some means a part or portion of a whole

explanation.surface: A politician's role being filled by a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' suggests the political party, but means generous, as in a handsome gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome can mean generous or ample, as in a handsome donation.

clue.text: Rather splendid end

explanation.surface: A fairly grand conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a pun: 'rather splendid' is fine-ish, which runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word puns on a near-'fine' quality and also means a conclusion.

clue.text: Smoke in church and a large number will be furious

parts.note: incense is the fragrant smoke burned during church services
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Fumes in a crowded church will make people angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Incensed means enraged, very angry.
